subject.title: [Feature]: Lightweight subagent instruction files (à la Claude Code .claude/agents/)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core `sessions_spawn` role-file convention for lightweight subagents, or should this remain in existing `agents.list`, bootstrap, skill, or plugin surfaces?
rationale: This is a new trusted prompt/config surface affecting role identity, model choice, tool policy, auditability, and possible memory write-back semantics, so code inspection alone cannot choose the permanent product boundary.

options.title: Design a core role-file feature
options.body: Add a narrow label-backed role-file contract with explicit precedence, no capability expansion from file frontmatter unless approved, loaded-file audit metadata, and focused docs/tests.

options.title: Defer to existing agent configuration
options.body: Keep the issue open only as a docs/workflow gap around `agents.list`, bootstrap files, attachments, and `agents.defaults.subagents` until maintainers confirm no new core surface is needed.

options.title: Prototype through plugin or ClawHub
options.body: Route the convention to a plugin or bundle-style package if current extension points can inject the role context without adding one-off core behavior.

recommendation.title: Design a core role-file feature
recommendation.body: Add a narrow label-backed role-file contract with explicit precedence, no capability expansion from file frontmatter unless approved, loaded-file audit metadata, and focused docs/tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across subagent orchestration, prompt assembly, config schema helpers, and the affected runtime files.
